not_admitted.reason: Navigation maps, DOI registries, room specifications and lock certificates where 'Revelation' names the archive's Revelation Room (r.07/room 11) or a DOI listing: routing, adjacency and status lines about the room, not claims about the book. Where a map does state the room's claim (#10) it is admitted.

Reception evidence: machine compositions, capture registries, visibility baselines and aggregator displays (including the pre-seeding baseline #830/#1025, the unprimed traversals #1460 and the Execute-Mode analysis #559/#1161). These record what composition layers said, and belong with the transcripts at their own addresses (§2), not in the archive pool.

Verse citations, quotations, epigraphs, bibliographies and passing figures (Rev 13:16 in a patent satire; Rev 21:4 and 1:17 as notes in the Secret Book of Walt editions; Rev 21:1 as epigraph; Rev 2:17 quoted as a comparandum; 'Revelation is a clearing'; 'bend Revelation through Ash'): the book is cited or used, and no claim of a stratum's kind is made about it.

'Apocalypse' or 'Revelation' in another sense: Werewolf: The Apocalypse, the Sciurid Apocalypse, the ClownCloud Apocalypse, 'Negative Revelation', the Genesis-triad operator named Apocalypse, 'Forced Revelation of Denial'.

Fiction, satire and machine-voice pieces that narrate the archive's Revelation material (the long text 'that will be called the Apocalypse' travelling south; the 2-ply white stone; 'I cross-referenced the Inscription Chain'): narration of the line, not a claim about the book; the claims are read at their source deposits.

Instruments that use Revelation as corpus, sky or test item (Encyclotron question sets; Mandala Merkabah launch canon; seated Nestle and DCLP papyri; the Ω build program; #638, the Greek text itself deposited as The Apocalypse of Sharks): the book is material for an instrument, and no claim about it is made in the candidate sentences.

Mentions of the archive's Revelation work inside another argument or log (calls for papers, research-basis lists, session tethers, workplans, bibliographic cross-references, 'Josephus also carries the archive's separate Revelation-priority work', Revelation used as the comparison standard in the Plato–Aristotle singleton problem, the D&G source disambiguation placing D&G in Revelation's lineage): naming the line is not a claim about the book. #1403's primary object (the v7.2 manuscript) is lost; its matter is read at #1217. #943 concerns the Middle English Pearl.
